docs.title: vexy-pdf3md
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md converts one PDF, or every PDF in a folder tree, to Markdown. It runs locally and calls no cloud OCR or AI service.

You can name a converter, let the package choose one, or run several converters side by side and compare the results. When a converter fails, the package tries another eligible one. Each result records every attempt and the converter that produced the file.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
You give the tool a PDF file or a folder:

vexy-pdf3md book.pdf

The tool writes book.md beside the PDF and prints a JSON report to stdout:

{
  "ok": true,
  "succeeded": 1,
  "skipped": 0,
  "failed": 0,
  "results": [
    {
      "input": "/path/to/book.pdf",
      "output": "/path/to/book.md",
      "requested": "auto",
      "status": "success",
      "strategy": "pymupdf",
      "attempts": [{"strategy": "pymupdf", "status": "success", "seconds": 0.308, "error": ""}],
      "error": ""
    }
  ]
}

requested is the strategy you asked for. strategy is the converter that actually wrote the file. attempts lists every converter that was tried, in order.

docs.title: Converters
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md does not convert PDFs itself. It calls one of five converters, called strategies:

Strategy Kind How it is found markit Text layer, column-aware markit executable on PATH pymupdf Text layer, basic blocks and headings Always available (core dependency) pdf22md macOS PDFKit text and Apple Vision OCR pdf22md executable on PATH tesseract OCR of rendered pages tesseract executable on PATH docling Layout and table reconstruction, OCR docling extra installed

PyMuPDF is a core dependency, so a fresh install can already convert PDFs that have a text layer.

  • Output layout and media: file names, suffixes, media folders and overwrite rules.
  • Python API: convert() and the result objects.
  • Architecture: the worker processes, timeouts and staged writes.
  • Troubleshooting: common failures and what to do.
  • Development and release: tests, builds and publishing.

docs.title: License
docs.text: The package's own code is licensed under Apache-2.0. Dependencies keep their own licenses. PyMuPDF is under AGPL or a commercial license.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The package exports one function and four data classes:

from vexy_pdf3md import Attempt, BatchResult, Options, Result, __version__, convert

docs.title: convert()
docs.text:
def convert(
    input: str | Path,
    output: str | Path | None = None,
    strategies: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] = "auto",
    media: bool | str = False,
    workers: int = 2,
    timeout: float = 600,
    fallback: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    pages: str = "",
    password: str = "",
    lang: str = "eng",
    dpi: int = 150,
    ocr: str = "auto",
    min_text_ratio: float = 0.5,
) -> BatchResult

The arguments mean the same as the command-line options. Differences:

  • strategies may be a comma-separated string ("markit,pymupdf"), "all", or a list or tuple of names.
  • media accepts True (same as "images"), False (same as "none"), "images", "pages" or "none".

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Configuration and path problems raise before any conversion starts:

  • ValueError for invalid options (for example workers=0, dpi=50, an unknown strategy), an input that is not a .pdf file or folder, a folder with no PDFs, or an output collision;
  • FileNotFoundError (an OSError) when input does not exist.

Failures of individual documents do not raise. They are returned in the BatchResult.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from vexy_pdf3md import convert

batch = convert("pdfs", "markdown", strategies="auto", media=True, workers=4)
for item in batch.results:
    print(item.input, item.output, item.status, item.strategy)
    for attempt in item.attempts:
        print(attempt.strategy, attempt.status, attempt.error)
assert batch.ok

docs.title: BatchResult
docs.text:
Member Type Meaning results list[Result] One entry per output file ok bool (property) True when no result has status "failed" to_dict() dict The JSON report the CLI prints

to_dict() returns:

{
    "ok": True,
    "succeeded": 1,   # results with status "success"
    "skipped": 0,     # results with status "skipped"
    "failed": 0,      # results with status "failed"
    "results": [...], # each Result as a dict
}

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Field Type Meaning input str Absolute path of the source PDF output str Path of the Markdown file requested str Strategy requested for this job ("auto" or a name) status "success", "failed", "skipped" Outcome strategy str or None Converter that wrote the file; None if none did attempts list[Attempt] Every converter tried, in order error str Error for a failed document; empty otherwise

docs.title: Attempt
docs.text: Field Type Meaning strategy str Converter name status "success" or "failed" Outcome of this attempt seconds float Duration, rounded to milliseconds error str Failure message; the password is replaced with [redacted]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Options is a frozen data class holding the validated settings. convert() builds it for you; constructing it directly is useful to check settings without converting:

from vexy_pdf3md import Options

Options(strategies=("pymupdf",), workers=4)    # valid
Options(strategies=("auto", "markit"))         # ValueError: auto must stand alone

Fields and their checks:

Field Default Check strategies ("auto",) Non-empty, unique names; auto alone media "none" "none", "images" or "pages" workers 2 Integer, 1 to 64 timeout 600 Finite and positive fallback True Boolean overwrite False Boolean pages "" String password "" String; hidden from repr() lang "eng" Names at least one language dpi 150 Integer, 72 to 600 ocr "auto" "auto", "always" or "never" min_text_ratio 0.5 0 to 1

docs.title: __version__
docs.text: The installed version string, generated from the Git tag at build time by hatch-vcs.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: vexy-pdf3md is about 1,000 lines of Python in src/vexy_pdf3md/. This page follows one PDF through the code.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module Role cli.py Fire CLI: logging setup, JSON report, exit status converter.py convert(): builds options, plans jobs, runs them, collects attempts models.py Options, Attempt, Result, BatchResult; strategy names paths.py Plans input → output pairs and rejects collisions process.py Starts worker processes, enforces timeouts, kills process groups worker.py Worker entry point: inspect, convert or export media inspection.py Page selection, scan detection, temporary page-limited PDF selection.py Candidate ranking and output quality checks backends.py Adapters for markit, PyMuPDF, pdf22md, Tesseract and Docling languages.py Maps --lang codes and fetches Tesseract models media.py Renders images or pages and builds the ## Media section publication.py Moves finished files into place

docs.title: One PDF, step by step
docs.text:
Take vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --media.

  1. Validate. convert() turns the arguments into an Options object. Invalid values raise ValueError; the CLI prints the error and exits with status 2.
  2. Plan. paths.plan() resolves book.pdf, chooses book.md, and checks for collisions. The result is a list of Job(source, output, requested) entries.
  3. Schedule. A thread pool of --workers threads runs the jobs. The threads do no PDF work; each one waits on worker processes.
  4. Inspect. A worker process runs inspection.inspect() and returns a profile: selected pages, character counts per page, pages that look scanned, and whether the document needs OCR.
  5. Rank. selection.candidates() turns the profile and options into an ordered list of converters.
  6. Attempt. For each candidate, a new worker process writes result.md into a temporary folder (named .pdf3md-*) next to book.md. The parent reads it and runs check_quality(). On failure the error is recorded and the next candidate is tried.
  7. Media. After a successful attempt, another worker renders the images into the temporary folder and returns the ## Media Markdown, which is appended.
  8. Publish. publication.publish() moves the media folder into place first, then the Markdown file. The Markdown is the commit point: without --overwrite it is created with a hard link, so an existing file is never replaced.

docs.title: Why worker processes
docs.text:
PyMuPDF must not be used from several threads at once, and native converters (Docling in particular) can crash the process on some scans. A Python exception handler cannot catch a segmentation fault. So all PDF work — inspection, conversion and media rendering — runs in a child process started as python -m vexy_pdf3md.worker RESPONSE.json.

The request, including any password, is sent on the worker's stdin as JSON. The worker writes its answer to the response file, not stdout, so library output cannot corrupt it. Worker stdout and stderr go to worker.log; the last part of that log is included in the error if the worker exits without a response.

docs.title: Timeouts and cancellation
docs.text:
Each worker gets --timeout seconds. On POSIX systems the worker starts in its own session; on timeout or Ctrl-C the whole process group is killed with SIGKILL, including converter subprocesses such as markit or tesseract. On Windows only the direct worker process is killed.

If the batch is interrupted, a shared cancel flag is set. Workers that are running are killed within about 0.2 seconds, and jobs that have not started a worker yet do not start one.

docs.title: Staged writes
docs.text: All files are written to a temporary folder beside the destination first. If a conversion fails, nothing at the destination changes. If moving the new media folder into place fails, the previous media folder is restored from a backup.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Release versions come from Git tags. The full history is in CHANGELOG.md and the Git log.

docs.title: Documentation and packaging
docs.text:
• Documentation site built from src_docs/md/ with ProperDocs and fly-january 0.3.0 or later (chrome: none), published at https://vexy.dev/vexy-pdf3md/.
  • build.sh builds the documentation and the package. publish.sh dispatches the GitHub Actions release workflow, which publishes to PyPI through Trusted Publishing.

docs.title: Conversion
docs.text:
• Text layers made of control codes (subset fonts without ToUnicode) are detected as scanned pages. Text-layer converters' output of this kind is rejected, and Docling runs in full-page OCR mode for such documents.
  • --strategies=all runs every strategy side by side.
  • --language and --vision-languages are replaced by one --lang list (pl,en or pol+eng) used by Tesseract, Docling and pdf22md Vision.
  • Missing Tesseract models are downloaded from tessdata_fast into ~/.cache/vexy-pdf3md/tessdata. Output configs are mirrored there so Docling's TSV parsing still works with --tessdata-dir. Parallel workers stage downloads in separate files.
  • Docling: requires pydantic 2.12 or later, and a torchaudio build that fails to load is replaced by a stub.
  • A document is routed to OCR only when at least 20% of the selected pages look scanned. Isolated image pages log a warning instead.
  • A failed strategy in a multi-strategy run no longer falls back to a sibling strategy. A warning names the converter whenever it differs from the requested one.
  • New all extra.

docs.title: Initial release
docs.text:
• Fire CLI (vexy-pdf3md, pdf3md, python -m vexy_pdf3md) and Python API.
  • Single-file and recursive-tree conversion, strategy suffixes, and generated media folders with relative links.
  • Adapters for markit, PyMuPDF, pdf22md, Tesseract and optional Docling.
  • Scan-aware routing, fallback, text-retention checks, operation timeouts, native-crash isolation, bounded concurrency and per-attempt JSON reports.
  • Page selection, passwords, OCR controls and languages, DPI and overwrite policy.
  • Staged publication, collision detection, media ownership checks, and preservation of previous output when publication fails.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md INPUT [--output=OUTPUT] [--strategies=auto] [--media=False] [options]

pdf3md and python -m vexy_pdf3md accept the same arguments. The CLI is built with Python Fire, so:

  • INPUT can be given as the first positional argument or as --input=INPUT.
  • Options accept both --name=value and --name value.
  • Option names with underscores also accept hyphens: --min_text_ratio and --min-text-ratio are the same option.
  • vexy-pdf3md --help prints the full option list.

docs.title: Arguments and options
docs.text: Option Short Default Meaning INPUT / --input required PDF file, or folder searched recursively for .pdf files (any case) --output beside the input Markdown file or output folder --strategies -s auto auto, all, or comma-separated names from markit,pymupdf,pdf22md,tesseract,docling --media False True or images: export raster images. pages: render whole pages. False or none: no media --workers -w 2 Maximum simultaneous jobs, 1 to 64 --timeout -t 600 Seconds allowed for each inspection, converter attempt, or media export --fallback -f True Try another converter after a failure --overwrite False Replace existing Markdown and media folders this package created --pages all pages One-based, inclusive page selection, for example 1-3,5 --password empty Password for encrypted PDFs. Never written to reports or logs --lang -l eng OCR language hints as ISO 639-1 or Tesseract codes, for example pl,en or pol+eng --dpi -d 150 Resolution for OCR and media rendering, 72 to 600 --ocr auto auto detects scans, always requires OCR, never uses text layers only --min_text_ratio 0.5 Minimum share of the PDF's text layer the output must keep, 0 to 1 --verbose -v False Print converter diagnostics to stderr

docs.title: --strategies
docs.text:
• auto lets the package rank the installed converters. See Strategies and fallback.
  • A single name, such as --strategies=pymupdf, tries that converter first.
  • Several names, such as --strategies=markit,pymupdf, run each converter as an independent job and add a .STRATEGY.md suffix to each output file.
  • all is shorthand for all five names.
  • auto cannot be combined with other names, and a name cannot appear twice.

docs.title: --pages
docs.text:
Pages are numbered from 1. Ranges are inclusive. The selection is sorted and duplicates are removed, so 5,1-3,2 selects pages 1, 2, 3 and 5. A range outside the document, such as 1-90 on a 40-page PDF, fails that document with page range '1-90' is outside 1-40.

When --pages or --password is used, the tool first writes a temporary, unencrypted copy containing only the selected pages, so every converter sees exactly the same pages.

docs.title: --lang
docs.text:
Give one list for all OCR converters. Each entry may be an ISO 639-1 code (pl, en, zh-hant) or a Tesseract model name (pol, eng, chi_tra). Entries may be separated by commas or +. The list is mapped to:

  • Tesseract -l codes, for example pl,en becomes pol+eng;
  • Docling's Tesseract OCR options;
  • pdf22md --languages codes for Apple Vision, for example pol,eng becomes pl,en.

Unknown codes are passed through unchanged, so any installed Tesseract model can be named.

docs.title: --media
docs.text:
Value Result False, none No media folder True, images Each displayed raster image region is rendered to PNG pages Each selected page is rendered to PNG, including vector artwork

See Output layout and media.

docs.title: --ocr
docs.text:
• auto: every selected page is inspected. The document is sent to OCR converters only when at least 20% of the selected pages look scanned.
  • always: only OCR converters (pdf22md, tesseract, docling) are used.
  • never: tesseract is removed from the candidates, and Docling runs with OCR turned off. pdf22md runs in its --fast mode, without Vision OCR.

docs.title: --timeout
docs.text: The limit applies to each operation separately: the inspection, each converter attempt, and the media export. A fallback chain can therefore take longer in total than one timeout.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text:
The CLI prints a JSON batch report to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr.

Exit status Meaning 0 Every output succeeded or was skipped 1 At least one conversion failed 2 Invalid options or input path; nothing was converted

For exit status 2, the report is a single line with the error:

$ vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --workers=0
{"ok": false, "error": "workers must be an integer from 1 to 64"}

A PDF that fails to convert does not stop the other jobs in the batch.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# book.pdf -> book.md, beside the PDF
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf

# Explicit output file, with images in ./results/renamed/
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --output results/renamed.md --media

# Map a tree of PDFs to a tree of Markdown files
vexy-pdf3md ./pdfs --output ./markdown --workers=4

# Run two converters side by side, with images
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --strategies=markit,pymupdf --media

# OCR selected pages with Polish and English hints, full-page images
vexy-pdf3md scan.pdf --strategies=tesseract --pages=1-3,5 --lang=pl,en --media=pages --dpi=200

# Every converter side by side
vexy-pdf3md scan.pdf --strategies=all --lang=pl,en

# Docling, from a checkout
uv run --extra docling vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --strategies=docling

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and enter it.

  2. Create the environment with the development tools:

    uv sync

    The dev dependency group adds pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, ty, hatchling and hatch-vcs.

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
./test.sh

test.sh runs, in order:

  1. ruff check on src, tests and examples;
  2. ruff format --check on the same folders;
  3. ty check src (with the docling extra, so the Docling adapter type-checks);
  4. pytest --cov with a coverage gate of 80%;
  5. examples/smoke.py.

Arguments to test.sh are passed to pytest, for example ./test.sh -k languages.

Other test commands:

uv run --extra docling pytest -m optional   # real Docling run; may download models
uvx hatch test                              # isolated hatch test environment

Tests marked optional need Docling and model downloads and are excluded by default (addopts = "-ra -m 'not optional'" in pyproject.toml).

docs.title: Test layout
docs.text: File Covers tests/test_conversion.py Conversion contracts with real PDFs and isolated workers tests/test_strategies.py Real converter integrations and injected converter failures tests/test_failures.py Publication, process boundaries and path conflicts failing without data loss tests/test_languages.py --lang mapping and Tesseract model handling tests/test_release.py Release workflow dispatch and error handling

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The version comes from Git tags through hatch-vcs. During a build or install, hatch-vcs writes src/vexy_pdf3md/__version__.py; that file is listed in .gitignore and must not be committed. After you change tags, rebuild or reinstall to refresh the version of an editable install.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only, into docs/
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, then twine check

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation source is src_docs/md/, configured by src_docs/mkdocs.yml. src_docs/build.sh uses Python 3.13, ProperDocs and fly-january 0.3.0 or later with extra.fly.chrome set to none. GitHub Pages serves the generated docs/ directory at https://vexy.dev/vexy-pdf3md/.

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

The Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) rebuilds docs/ on every push to main that changes src_docs/ and commits the result.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
The PyPI project owner must configure a GitHub trusted publisher for vexyart/vexy-pdf3md, workflow release.yml, environment pypi.

  1. Run ./test.sh and push the release commit to the default branch.
  2. With the GitHub CLI authenticated for this repository, run ./publish.sh for the next patch version, or pass an explicit tag such as ./publish.sh v1.4.0.
  3. Check the Release workflow in GitHub Actions. The workflow creates the tag if needed, builds the wheel and sdist from that tag, and attaches them to the GitHub release. Its pypi job uploads the same artifacts using GitHub's OIDC identity.

Pushing a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag directly also triggers the Release workflow.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later.
  • uv for the commands shown on this page.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
Install from PyPI:

uv tool install vexy-pdf3md
vexy-pdf3md --help

To install with the Docling converter included:

uv tool install 'vexy-pdf3md[docling]'

The all extra currently installs the same set as docling.

docs.title: Install from a checkout
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and enter it:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-pdf3md.git
cd vexy-pdf3md

  2. Create the environment:

    uv sync

  3. Run the CLI from the checkout:

    uv run vexy-pdf3md --help

  4. Optional: install the checkout as a CLI that works outside the repository:

    uv tool install .
# or, with Docling:
uv tool install '.[docling]'

docs.title: Commands installed
docs.text:
The package installs the same command under two names:

  • vexy-pdf3md
  • pdf3md

python -m vexy_pdf3md runs the same CLI.

docs.title: Optional converters
docs.text: PyMuPDF is installed with the package and works immediately for PDFs with a text layer. The other converters are optional. The package looks for them on PATH, or, for Docling, checks whether the docling Python package can be imported.

docs.title: markit
docs.text: Install from the upstream instructions. vexy-pdf3md runs it as markit -q --no-images FILE.pdf. markit is the first choice for text-layer PDFs and handles multi-column layouts.

docs.title: pdf22md (macOS)
docs.text: Build and install pdf22md. It provides PDFKit text extraction and Apple Vision OCR. It is the first choice for scanned PDFs when it is installed.

docs.title: Tesseract
docs.text:
On macOS:

brew install tesseract

On other systems, install your distribution's Tesseract package.

Language models named by --lang that are not in the system tessdata folder are downloaded from tessdata_fast into ~/.cache/vexy-pdf3md/tessdata on first use. If XDG_CACHE_HOME is set, the cache is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/vexy-pdf3md/tessdata instead. To work offline, install the language packs with your package manager, for example:

brew install tesseract-lang

docs.title: Docling
docs.text:
From a checkout:

uv sync --extra docling
uv run --extra docling vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --strategies=docling

The extra requires docling>=2.126,<3 and pydantic>=2.12. The Docling adapter uses Tesseract for OCR when tesseract is on PATH. Docling may download layout and table models on first use.

docs.title: Check what is available
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md has no separate "list converters" command. To see which external tools are on your PATH:

which markit pdf22md tesseract
tesseract --list-langs

Automatic selection only uses converters that are installed. If you name a missing converter with --strategies, that attempt fails and the next eligible converter is tried (unless --fallback=False).

docs.title: Where Markdown files go
docs.text: The output path is planned for every job before any conversion starts.

docs.title: Single PDF
docs.text:
--output Result for book.pdf not given book.md beside the PDF notes.md notes.md an existing folder out/ out/book.md anything else not ending in .md error, exit status 2

The input file must end in .pdf (any letter case). If the input is a symbolic link to a PDF, the link is resolved and the target is converted.

docs.title: Folder of PDFs
docs.text:
The folder is searched recursively for files ending in .pdf, .PDF and so on. Each PDF maps to the same relative path under --output, with the extension changed to .md. Without --output, each Markdown file goes next to its PDF.

--output is always treated as a folder for folder input, even if its name ends in .md. If --output names an existing file, the run stops with exit status 2.

Symbolic links to folders are not followed, and symbolic links to PDF files inside the tree are skipped. A folder with no PDFs is an error.

docs.title: Several strategies
docs.text:
When more than one strategy is requested, each output gets a suffix with the requested strategy name:

pdfs/part/book.PDF
  --output markdown
    -> markdown/part/book.md
  --output markdown --strategies=markit,pymupdf --media
    -> markdown/part/book.markit.md
       markdown/part/book.markit/page-0001-001.png
    -> markdown/part/book.pymupdf.md
       markdown/part/book.pymupdf/page-0001-001.png

The suffix names the strategy you asked for, even if a fallback converter wrote the file. The JSON report's strategy field names the converter that actually did.

docs.title: Media export
docs.text:
With --media (or --media=images), each raster image region shown on a page is rendered to PNG at --dpi. With --media=pages, each selected page is rendered as a whole, which includes vector artwork. The images are rendered pixels: original embedded image formats, editable vectors and exact inline placement are not kept.

The images go into a folder named after the Markdown file's full stem, next to it:

book.md
book/
  .vexy-pdf3md
  page-0001-001.png
  page-0003-001.png
  page-0003-002.png

File names are page-PPPP-NNN.png: the one-based page number in the original PDF, then the image number on that page. A ## Media section is appended to the Markdown, with one relative, URL-escaped link per image:

## Media

![Page 1, image 1](book/page-0001-001.png)

The media folder is created even if no images are found. The .vexy-pdf3md file marks the folder as generated by this package.

docs.title: Existing files and overwrite
docs.text:
• Existing Markdown is skipped by default. The result has "status": "skipped" and the exit status stays 0.
  • --overwrite=True replaces the Markdown only after the new conversion has passed the quality checks. If conversion fails, the old file stays.
  • An existing media folder is replaced only with --overwrite=True and only if it contains the .vexy-pdf3md marker. Otherwise the job fails with media directory already exists and is not replaceable. Keep hand-made files outside generated media folders.
  • If installing the new media folder fails, the previous one is restored.

docs.title: Collision checks
docs.text:
Before converting, the tool rejects plans where:

  • two jobs would write the same path, compared case-insensitively (for example A.pdf and a.PDF in one folder);
  • an output path is the same as an input PDF;
  • an output path is a symbolic link;
  • one output path is inside another job's media folder.

These checks cover one invocation. Do not run two invocations that write the same destinations at the same time.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page walks through the common tasks. The examples assume vexy-pdf3md is on your PATH. From a checkout, prefix each command with uv run.

docs.title: Convert one PDF
docs.text:
1. Run the tool on the file:

    vexy-pdf3md book.pdf

  2. Read the JSON report on stdout. "ok": true means the conversion succeeded or was skipped.

Result: book.md is written beside book.pdf.

If book.md already exists, the file is skipped and reported with "status": "skipped". Add --overwrite=True to replace it.

docs.title: Choose the output file
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --output results/renamed.md

Result: results/renamed.md. For a single input file, --output may also be an existing folder; the file is then written as FOLDER/book.md.

docs.title: Convert a folder tree
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md ./pdfs --output ./markdown --workers=4

The tool finds every file ending in .pdf (any letter case) under ./pdfs, and writes each Markdown file to the same relative path under ./markdown:

pdfs/part/book.PDF  ->  markdown/part/book.md

Up to four PDFs are converted at the same time. Omit --output to write each Markdown file next to its PDF.

docs.title: Export images
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --media

Result:

book.md
book/page-0001-001.png
book/.vexy-pdf3md

book.md ends with a ## Media section that links each PNG. Use --media=pages to render whole pages, including vector artwork, instead of only raster images. See Output layout and media.

docs.title: Compare converters
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --strategies=markit,pymupdf

Result: book.markit.md and book.pymupdf.md, one per strategy. Use --strategies=all to run all five. Add --fallback=False when you want each file to come only from the named converter.

docs.title: Convert a scan
docs.text:
vexy-pdf3md scan.pdf --strategies=tesseract --pages=1-3,5 --lang=pl,en --dpi=200

This OCRs pages 1, 2, 3 and 5 with Tesseract, using Polish and English models, at 200 dpi. In automatic mode you usually do not need --strategies: a PDF whose pages look scanned is routed to an OCR converter. See Strategies and fallback.

docs.title: Use the Python API
docs.text:
from vexy_pdf3md import convert

batch = convert("pdfs", "markdown", strategies="auto", media=True, workers=4)
print(batch.ok)
for item in batch.results:
    print(item.input, item.output, item.status, item.strategy)

See Python API.

docs.title: Run the bundled example
docs.text:
From a checkout:

uv run examples/smoke.py

The script creates a one-page PDF in a temporary folder, converts it with strategies="pymupdf" and media="pages", and checks that the text and the page image were written. It prints:

Verified nested/example.md and its rendered page image.

docs.title: Strategies and fallback
docs.text: This page explains how vexy-pdf3md picks a converter, when it rejects a result, and what happens next.

docs.title: Step 1: inspect the PDF
docs.text:
Before any conversion, a worker process opens the PDF with PyMuPDF and checks every selected page. A page is marked as looks scanned when any of these is true:

  • it has fewer than 40 letters or digits in its text layer and an image covers more than 20% of the page;
  • it has no text at all but contains vector drawings;
  • more than 5% of its text (and more than 3 characters) is the replacement character U+FFFD;
  • its text layer is mostly control codes. This happens with subset fonts that have no ToUnicode map: the text layer has characters but no readable words.

The document needs OCR only when at least 20% of the selected pages look scanned. If some pages look scanned but fewer than 20%, the tool logs a warning naming those pages and uses the text layer. Pass --ocr=always to OCR such a document anyway.

docs.title: Step 2: rank the candidates
docs.text:
The candidate order depends on whether the document needs OCR:

Document Order Text layer markit → pymupdf → pdf22md → tesseract → docling Needs OCR, or --ocr=always pdf22md → tesseract → docling

With --ocr=never, tesseract is removed from the list.

docs.title: --strategies=auto
docs.text:
Only installed converters are kept, in the order above. pymupdf is always installed. If a scanned document has no installed OCR converter, the document fails with:

scanned PDF needs an OCR tool: install pdf22md, Tesseract, or vexy-pdf3md[docling]

docs.title: A named strategy
docs.text: The named converter is tried first, even if it is not installed (the attempt then fails with markit is not installed or not on PATH, or similar). The installed converters from the ranked list follow as fallbacks.

docs.title: Several named strategies
docs.text: Each named converter gets its own job and its own output file. A failed job never falls back to one of its siblings, because that sibling already writes its own file and the fallback would only produce a duplicate under a misleading suffix. Fallback goes to converters you did not name.

docs.title: --fallback=False
docs.text: Only the first candidate is tried. Use this for strict comparisons between converters.

docs.title: Step 3: convert and check the result
docs.text:
Each attempt runs in a separate worker process. An attempt fails when:

  • the worker crashes, exits with a nonzero status, or exceeds --timeout;
  • an external converter exits with a nonzero status;
  • the document needs OCR and the converter only reads the text layer (markit, pymupdf);
  • the converter is tesseract and --ocr=never is set;
  • the output has no letters or digits;
  • the output is mostly control codes;
  • more than 2% of the output (and more than 3 characters) is U+FFFD;
  • the output keeps fewer letters and digits than --min_text_ratio times the count in the PDF's text layer (default: half).

The text checks ignore HTML comments and Markdown image links, and they run before media is appended.

When an attempt fails, its error is recorded in attempts and the next candidate is tried. When every candidate fails, the result has "status": "failed" and "error": "all conversion strategies failed".

If the converter that succeeded is not the one you named, a warning is printed:

book.pdf: markit failed; pymupdf wrote /path/to/book.markit.md

docs.title: markit
docs.text: Runs markit -q --no-images FILE.pdf and reads stdout.

docs.title: pymupdf
docs.text: Built in. Extracts text blocks page by page. The most common font size (weighted by characters) is treated as body text. Up to six larger sizes (more than 15% above body size) become heading levels # to ######. Pages are separated by ---. It does not reconstruct tables.

docs.title: pdf22md
docs.text: Runs pdf22md --input FILE --output native.md --quiet --languages CODES --dpi DPI. --fast is added when OCR is not needed or --ocr=never is set.

docs.title: tesseract
docs.text: Renders each page to PNG at --dpi and runs tesseract PAGE.png stdout -l CODES --tessdata-dir DIR on it. Pages are separated by ---. Missing language models are downloaded on first use (see Installation).

docs.title: docling
docs.text: Runs Docling's DocumentConverter with OCR enabled unless --ocr=never. When tesseract is on PATH, Docling uses Tesseract with the --lang codes, at a scale of --dpi / 72. For documents that need OCR, or with --ocr=always, it OCRs whole pages; otherwise only bitmap regions.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Scan detection and length checks are heuristics. They cannot prove that OCR is complete or correct. Exporting page images does not count as a successful conversion: an image-only document still needs usable OCR text.

docs.title: Measured comparison
docs.text:
The project measured all five strategies on 123 Microsoft localization style guides: text-layer PDFs of 30 to 100 pages, 59 of them in non-Latin scripts. Only English OCR models were installed, so the OCR ratings describe text-layer input, not scans.

Strategy Observed markit Default choice. Keeps tables, reflows paragraphs, drops running headers and footers. Lost 4–22% of Greek and Indic letters (conjuncts, pre-base vowels), joins hyphenated words, shows 312x90pt image placeholders, may emit U+FFFD for fonts without Unicode maps. pymupdf Most complete text. Keeps every mapped glyph, font-size headings, page footers and hard line breaks. No tables. Missed inline Cyrillic runs in one Serbian guide that markit recovered. pdf22md Same text as the PyMuPDF layer, but one line per text run, no headings or tables, footers kept. When routing forced OCR, Vision turned Cyrillic into Latin lookalikes. tesseract On text PDFs, about 5% of words lost and 8% garbage on Latin scripts; non-Latin scripts unreadable without language packs. Use it for real scans. docling Not rated: it was not installed during the run, so every .docling.md file was a markit fallback. This result led to the no-sibling-fallback rule above.

markit gave the best result for 110 documents. PyMuPDF was better for the Greek guide and ten Indic guides where markit dropped letters, and for two Bengali and Konkani guides whose fonts lack Unicode maps. One Kyrgyz guide was sent to OCR because of a single screenshot page; the 20% page-share threshold now prevents that.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with --verbose. It prints each converter failure to stderr. The JSON report also lists every attempt with its error.

docs.title: The file was skipped
docs.text:
"status": "skipped"

The Markdown file already exists. Add --overwrite=True to replace it.

docs.title: media directory already exists and is not replaceable
docs.text: A folder with the Markdown file's stem already exists, and either --overwrite is not set or the folder has no .vexy-pdf3md marker. The tool does not delete folders it did not create. Move or rename the folder, then run again.

docs.title: scanned PDF needs an OCR tool
docs.text: At least 20% of the selected pages look scanned, and none of pdf22md, tesseract or Docling is installed. Install one of them (see Installation). If the document does have a usable text layer, run with --ocr=never.

docs.title: document needs OCR; this strategy only reads the text layer
docs.text: You named markit or pymupdf, but the document was classified as scanned (or you passed --ocr=always). The attempt fails and fallback moves on to OCR converters. To force text-layer extraction, add --ocr=never.

docs.title: A scanned page was not OCRed
docs.text:
The log shows:

book.pdf: pages [12] look scanned but the text layer is used; pass --ocr=always to OCR the whole document

Fewer than 20% of the selected pages looked scanned, so the text layer was used. Run again with --ocr=always, or use --pages to convert only the scanned part.

docs.title: truncated output: N characters vs M in text layer
docs.text:
The converter kept fewer than --min_text_ratio (default 0.5) of the letters and digits in the PDF's text layer. The next converter is tried. If you know the text layer contains material you do not need (for example hidden text), lower the ratio:

vexy-pdf3md book.pdf --min-text-ratio=0.3

docs.title: text layer is unreadable control codes
docs.text: The PDF uses subset fonts without a ToUnicode map. The text layer has characters but no words. Such pages are classified as scanned; install an OCR converter so they can be OCRed.

docs.title: converter returned replacement-character corruption
docs.text: The output contains too many U+FFFD characters (more than 2%), usually from fonts without Unicode maps. Try another strategy, for example --strategies=pymupdf, or an OCR strategy.

docs.title: markit is not installed or not on PATH
docs.text: The named external converter was not found. Check with which markit. The same message appears for pdf22md and tesseract. For Docling the message is docling is not installed; install vexy-pdf3md[docling].

docs.title: no Tesseract model for 'xyz' and download failed
docs.text: The language model named by --lang is not installed and could not be downloaded from tessdata_fast. Check the code (for example pol, not pl-PL), your network, or install the language pack locally. On macOS: brew install tesseract-lang.

docs.title: PDF needs a valid password
docs.text: The PDF is encrypted. Pass --password=.... The password is never written to the JSON report or logs; it appears as [redacted] in error messages.

docs.title: page range '1-90' is outside 1-40
docs.text: --pages names pages beyond the end of the document. Page numbers start at 1.

docs.title: output collision: PATH
docs.text: Two jobs would write the same file, compared case-insensitively, or an output would overwrite an input PDF. Rename one of the PDFs, or write to a different --output.

docs.title: The output file name has the wrong converter's suffix
docs.text: With several strategies, the suffix names the strategy you requested. If that converter failed, another one may have written the file; a warning names it and the report's strategy field records it. Use --fallback=False to prevent this.

docs.title: A run takes much longer than --timeout
docs.text: --timeout applies to each operation: the inspection, each converter attempt, and the media export. A document that falls back through several converters can take several timeouts.
